title: Reading the flat year
intro: Seven months, zero net movement — and three stories underneath it worth understanding.

steps.title: The surface
steps.body:
2026 so far: flexi-cap **+0.6%**, large-cap **−2.6%**, ELSS **−0.9%**. The average flexi-cap NAV is back exactly where January left it.

'Nothing happened this year' — to the NAV. Plenty happened to the investor: SIPs accumulated, discipline got tested, and the numbers below finally told the truth.

steps.title: The small-cap truth serum
steps.body:
> [!warn] Small caps: **−13.2%** this year, **−7.8%** over one year — and a three-year return of **5.5% a year, less than a liquid fund** over the same period.

That last number is the one the rally hid. Anyone 'riding the rally' for three years earned money-market returns with small-cap volatility. The question isn't whether to ride the next one — it's what allocation you'd have wanted through this.

steps.title: The patient counterpoint
steps.body: Parag Parikh Flexi Cap's cash: from a peak near **25%** down to **14–15%**, headed for single digits — a famously patient allocator deploying into weakness. The letter says it; **monthly portfolio disclosures will verify it**. Claims are checkable — check them.

steps.title: The bubble frame
steps.body:
On AI, the issue borrows Chollet: *'A bubble is not a property of the technology. It is a property of the people buying.'* A thing can be a bubble **even if the tech works and demand is real** — prices, not products, make bubbles.

The frame travels: it's the question to ask of every theme fund, PSU rally, and small-cap surge in this magazine's pages.

recap:
**Flat NAVs, busy truths.**

- Flexi +0.6%, large −2.6%, ELSS −0.9% — a testing year, not a losing one.
- Small caps' 3-year 5.5%/yr < liquid funds: volatility unpaid.
- PPFAS deploying cash 25% → single digits — verifiable in disclosures.
- Bubbles are made by buyers, not technologies.
